page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.large is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9T24 cores running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core tests scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited by the dual-core configuration, resulting in weak multi-core scores in stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory performance is mixed; while write bandwidth for large blocks and the PassMark memory score are average, read-only bandwidth for small blocks falls into the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively.

The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff between strong single-threaded execution and constrained multi-threaded capacity. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a dense memory allocation relative to its low vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. It is suitable for lightweight caching, single-threaded data processing, and basic memory-intensive applications that operate within a 2 Gbps network baseline.
